outline.description: This chapter introduces the core challenges of controlling large-scale text-to-image diffusion models and defines the two primary tasks the textbook aims to solve: subject-driven and controllable generation.
subtopics: Overview of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
The Ambiguity of Text Guidance
Subject-Driven Generation: Concept and Goals
Controllable Generation: Concept and Goals
The Fundamental Trade-off: Training Efficiency vs. Generalizability Preservation

outline.description: Before diving into the proposed method, this chapter reviews existing finetuning strategies and explains why traditional methods often fail to preserve the pretraining capabilities of diffusion models.
subtopics: Standard Gradient Descent Finetuning
Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA): Principles and Constraints
The Problem of Semantic Drift and Model Collapse
Measuring Preservation: Euclidean Distance vs. Structural Measures

outline.chapter_title: The Geometry of Neurons: Hyperspherical Energy
outline.description: This chapter explores the theoretical intuition behind Orthogonal Finetuning, focusing on the role of neuron directions and angular relationships in encoding semantic information.
subtopics: The Unit Hypersphere and Neuron Normalization
Defining Hyperspherical Energy (HE)
Angular Similarity vs. Magnitude: Which stores semantics?
Case Study: The 2D Fourier Transform Analogy (Phase vs. Magnitude)
The Relationship Between Hyperspherical Energy and Generalization

outline.description: This chapter details the mathematical formulation of OFT, explaining how orthogonal transformations can adapt a model while provably preserving its hyperspherical energy.
subtopics: The Principle of Orthogonal Transformation
The OFT Forward Pass: Mathematically Transforming Weights
Proof of Hyperspherical Energy Invariance
OFT as a Coordinate System Adjustment
Initialization Strategies for Stable Start

outline.description: Since computing orthogonal matrices can be expensive, this chapter focuses on the engineering techniques used to make OFT computationally feasible and parameter-efficient.
subtopics: Challenges of Standard Orthogonalization (Gram-Schmidt)
Cayley Parameterization: Generating Orthogonal Matrices via Skew-Symmetric Matrices
Block-Diagonal Parameterization for Efficiency
Complexity Analysis: OFT vs. LoRA
Block Sharing Strategies to Reduce Trainable Parameters

outline.chapter_title: Advanced Variants: COFT and Re-scaled OFT
outline.description: This chapter introduces extensions to the basic OFT framework that further improve stability and flexibility.
subtopics: Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning (COFT): The Radius Constraint
Implementing the Epsilon-Deviation Constraint via Projected Gradient Descent

The Role of the Diagonal Matrix D in Enhancing Flexibility
Comparing the Stability of OFT and COFT

outline.description: This chapter describes the experimental setup, the metrics used to evaluate success, and the performance of OFT across different tasks.
subtopics: Experimental Setup: Stable Diffusion v1.5

outline.description: The final chapter provides a critical comparison between OFT and other adaptation methods, discusses its architectural flexibility, and identifies remaining open research problems.
subtopics: OFT vs. LoRA: Low-Rank vs. Sparse Orthogonal Structures
